title: Persist the release suite per scenario, and let memory fail a run
impact: Two halves of one problem: a crash still destroyed the run, and a memory regression could not stop anything. #282 made the suite persist after each completed *repeat*, but the sqlite_async peer segfault it was written against fires at the Memory scenario — the fifteenth of sixteen, inside repeat 1 — so no repeat ever completed and nothing was ever written. Exps 260 and 261 each ran fourteen scenarios successfully and produced no artifact at all, which is the concrete reason the trend charts are sparse. `_runSuiteOnce` now reports after every scenario and the runner persists on each callback; `repeatCount` counts only repeats that finished, and the artifact gains `scenariosCompleted`/`scenarioTotal`/`partial` so a partial run self-excludes from trends the same way `gitDirty` and `--repeat=1` already do. Verified by SIGKILL during scenario 10 of 16: nine scenarios and 153 metrics survive where previously nothing did, with `repeatCount: 0` and `partial: true`. The rewrite also fixed live drift between the progress labels (`[1/15]`..`[14/15]` then `[15/16]`) by making `scenarioTotal()` the single source for both. Second half: `compareMemory` returns a `MemoryComparison` carrying wins/regressions/neutral and the regressed benchmark names alongside the table that has always rendered them, the runner prints a banner naming each, and `--fail-on-memory-regression` exits non-zero — closing the `per-benchmark RSS acceptance criteria` candidate open since 2026-05-02, where the criteria existed but the acceptance did not. Opt-in by design: a local run reports without failing, CI is where a gate belongs. Neither a missing `## Memory` section nor a missing baseline can fail a run, because a gate that fires on absent data gets disabled. Does not fix the peer crash itself, which also leaks its temp databases (~1.2 GB accumulated on the dev machine from two days of crashed runs) because the segfault skips the `finally` that removes them.
